newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at their highest level in almost two weeks on Monday, taking their cue from Wall street's improved performance in the last two days.
The AEX index finished up 8.25 points at 561.64 with most gains achieved on the opening, although prices received a late boost from a stronger start by shares in New York.
"Wall Street is again a positive stimulus to our market," said one dealer.
Gains were achieved across the board with shipping group Nedlloyd leading the way, soaring 6.00 guilders or 15 percent to a 1996 closing high of 45.50 on heavy turnover.
Nedlloyd and Britain's P&O earlier announced they would merge their container shipping businesses, reaping annual cost savings of $200 million.
"The market rewards restructuring stories," said a dealer, citing the strength in Unilever shares last week on news it planned to review non-performing businesses.
Retailer Ahold added 1.20 to 95.40 guilders, despite trading exclusive of a dividend of 0.26 guilders plus $0.13.
Another dealer reported strong buying of retailer Ahold due to a positive presentation to analysts last Friday and the decision of broker ING Barings to lift its earnings estimates.
One of the few leading Dutch companies to lose ground was brewer Heineken, which dropped 0.30 to 370.20 guilders ahead of its interim results on Friday.
"There might be some scope for disappointment," said a trader.
Dealers said Wall Street's finish would determine the direction of Dutch shares on Tuesday, adding that today's gains were achieved on low volumes.
But chartists were neutral to bullish, saying a break of 555 to 565 would confirm a bullish scenario.
